notes: Hard-Decisions (Anthus AI Solutions; self-funded consultancy that also sells Jev-alignment services: a conflict of interest to keep in mind): ProofWriter multi-hop reasoning, 3,600 problems (1,800 open-world + 1,800 closed-world), depth 0 (answer written in the text) to 5 (five chained rules). GPT-6 Luna here is the generative model through Chat Completions with reasoning none and a strict JSON schema, NOT the OpenAI Decisions API (Anthus: "OpenAI uses a specialized version of Luna"). GLiDE was rerun on 2026-10-03 at the request of Fastino's CEO and scored lower (76.4 vs 82.9 open-world); the cause is unexplained and both runs are kept. Open models ran on an Apple M1 Max laptop (MLX): latency is NOT stored (hosted vs laptop is not like-for-like). Clef and Perplexity decider are not on this board. Jev is highest on both tasks; accuracy is non-monotonic by depth for Jev on closed-world (76.3 at depth 4, 89.3 at depth 5).

claims.statement: Hard-Decisions: Jev answered 83.8% of open-world and 89.3% of closed-world ProofWriter problems correctly, the highest tested; its lead over GPT-6 Luna (reasoning off) is +4.3 points at depth 0 and +34.9 at depth 5 on the open-world task. "when Luna stated 99% or more, it was right 68.7% of the time on open-world problems" (68.1% closed-world; Jev at 99% or more: 99.4% and 98.5%), from a separate log-probability probe; Anthus also writes that by five inference steps Luna was at a coin flip. Anthus runs this for the generative Luna, not the OpenAI Decisions API.
claims.implication: Wins are task-shape dependent: Jev is strong on multi-hop rule application and OOD-light reasoning, and the generative baseline had no reasoning budget here.
